findings.evidenceJa: 体はガラクタ
findings.governingReading: Sakura experiences her body as junk or useless scrap.
findings.explanation: The English turns alienated worthlessness into the simpler fact of bodily breakage.

findings.evidenceJa: 頭はフワフワ
findings.governingReading: Sakura’s consciousness or head feels unmoored and floating.
findings.explanation: The English reduces dissociation to ordinary lightheadedness.

findings.highlight: cover her ears if her arms would move
findings.evidenceJa: この手が動くなら耳を塞ぎたかった
findings.governingReading: Sakura wishes her hands would move so she could cover her ears.
findings.explanation: The English changes her impaired hands into entire arms.

findings.highlight: She scratches the sheets with her fingers
findings.evidenceJa: 満足に動かない指で、引き裂くほどシーツを毟る
findings.governingReading: With fingers that barely function, Sakura claws the sheets hard enough to tear them.
findings.explanation: The English removes both her impairment and the destructive force.

findings.highlight: A past event, spoken of lightly
findings.evidenceJa: 淡々と語られる昔話
findings.governingReading: Rin relates the old story in an even, matter-of-fact manner.
findings.explanation: The English changes emotional neutrality into lightness.

findings.highlight: The event that happened four years ago
findings.evidenceJa: 夕暮れの校庭であった出来事
findings.governingReading: The shared memory occurred in the schoolyard at sunset four years earlier.
findings.explanation: The English removes both place and time-of-day atmosphere.

findings.evidenceJa: [ruby text=わたし char=2]彼女がいた事
findings.governingReading: The surface third-person “she” is read intimately as Sakura’s first-person “I.”
findings.explanation: The English replaces the focalization shift with a detached “another girl.”

findings.highlight: a plea that none can hear
findings.evidenceJa: 届くはずのない懇願を、聞こえない声で
findings.governingReading: Sakura forces out in an inaudible voice a plea that cannot possibly reach its target.
findings.explanation: The English states only that nobody can hear it, losing the failed attempt to reach Rin.

findings.highlight: The only thing she had an edge on
findings.evidenceJa: [ruby text=おもいで char=3]希少品
findings.governingReading: Her sole “rare item,” read as memory, had seemed her one advantage over Rin.
findings.explanation: The English removes the treasured-object surface and memory reading.

findings.evidenceJa: ただの記憶に貶められていく
findings.governingReading: The treasured rarity is progressively degraded into an ordinary memory.
findings.explanation: The English pluralizes it into recollections, weakening the singular possession being lost.

findings.evidenceJa: 聞きたくない
findings.governingReading: Sakura states directly that she does not want to hear the conversation.
findings.explanation: The English omits the sentence entirely.

findings.highlight: Using magical energy to bridge the gaps
findings.evidenceJa: [ruby text=せいしん char=2]魔力で補い
findings.governingReading: Sakura supplements her shredded nerves with magical energy, read as spirit or mind.
findings.explanation: The English preserves the magical mechanism but loses the psychological ruby reading.

findings.evidenceJa: 目を潰そうが
findings.governingReading: Even crushing or blinding her own eyes would not let Sakura escape the vision.
findings.explanation: The English turns imagined self-blinding into harmlessly covering her eyes.

findings.highlight: the last person she wants to hear them
findings.evidenceJa: 一番言ってほしくない人に
findings.governingReading: Rin thrusts the words at the person Sakura least wants them said to: Shirou.
findings.explanation: The English instead makes Shirou the person Sakura least wants to hear the words, confusing addressee and listener.

findings.evidenceJa: 明るい[ruby text=せかい char=2]居間
findings.governingReading: The distant bright living room is read as an entire world from which Sakura feels excluded.
findings.explanation: The English preserves only the figurative world and loses the physical room and its brightness.

findings.evidenceJa: 遠く、明るい居間
findings.governingReading: The living room feels distant as well as bright.
findings.explanation: The English removes spatial distance.

findings.evidenceJa: 目蓋が熱い
findings.governingReading: Sakura’s eyelids feel hot as she begins crying.
findings.explanation: The English again changes eyelids into eyes.

findings.evidenceJa: 彼女は一人泣いていた
findings.governingReading: Sakura discovers herself crying alone.
findings.explanation: The English omits her isolation.

findings.evidenceJa: 遠坂の魔術師としての責任
findings.governingReading: Sakura frames the matter as Rin’s responsibility in her capacity as a Tohsaka magus.
findings.explanation: The English makes Rin the magus belonging to “Tohsaka,” obscuring identity and house responsibility.

findings.highlight: trying to turn her only ally against her
findings.evidenceJa: 姉さんと同じ立場にさせようとする
findings.governingReading: Sakura believes Rin is trying to place Shirou in the same position Rin occupies.
findings.explanation: The English escalates shared moral positioning into actively turning Shirou against Sakura.

findings.highlight: She hates Tohsaka Rin for trying to induce him
findings.evidenceJa: 遠坂凛が、本当に酷いと思った
findings.governingReading: Sakura thinks Rin is truly awful for maneuvering Shirou toward abandoning her.
findings.explanation: The English replaces her judgment of Rin’s conduct with another statement of Sakura’s hatred.

findings.highlight: Her sister is saying she should disappear
findings.evidenceJa: わたしが消えればいいと姉さんは言う
findings.governingReading: Sakura paraphrases Rin as saying it would be good if Sakura disappeared.
findings.explanation: The English turns a desired outcome into a direct normative “should.”

findings.highlight: The girl also knows she should disappear
findings.evidenceJa: 自分が消えればそれでいいと判っている
findings.governingReading: Sakura believes that if she disappears, that will settle or solve matters.
findings.explanation: The English turns her outcome-based despair into an obligation to disappear.

findings.highlight: She doesn’t want to lose anything
findings.evidenceJa: もう失うのはイヤだ
findings.governingReading: Sakura cannot bear losing anyone or anything again.
findings.explanation: The English removes the recurrence and makes the refusal universally object-based.

findings.evidenceJa: 今まで温かかった人たち
findings.governingReading: Sakura resents people who have possessed warmth all along.
findings.explanation: The English turns their continuous privileged history into an inherent quality.

findings.evidenceJa: 彼らは“わたし”に反対しなかった
findings.governingReading: Sakura reasons that they did not oppose the quoted, objectified “me.”
findings.explanation: The English omits the object and the marked alienation from herself.

findings.evidenceJa: もう我慢なんてしない
findings.governingReading: Sakura says she will no longer restrain herself or endure it if even Shirou tries to erase her.
findings.explanation: The English changes abandoning restraint into an assertion of cruelty.

findings.evidenceJa: 先輩もこの手で
findings.governingReading: Her interrupted threat explicitly imagines doing something to Shirou with this hand.
findings.explanation: The English preserves the block but removes her own hand as the instrument.

findings.evidenceJa: 口から何度も吐き出した
findings.governingReading: Sakura repeatedly expels the blood from her mouth.
findings.explanation: The English reduces repeated vomiting or spitting out to one cough.

findings.highlight: The pain turns her wild imagination to blood
findings.evidenceJa: 苦しくて苦しくて、自分の妄想を血に変えて
findings.governingReading: In repeated suffering, Sakura figuratively transforms her own fantasies into blood.
findings.explanation: The English assigns the transformation to pain and removes her reflexive agency.

findings.evidenceJa: わたし、だめみたいです
findings.governingReading: Sakura tells the absent Shirou that she seems to be no good or beyond help.
findings.explanation: The English changes a judgment about her deteriorating self into unspecified inability.

findings.highlight: cannot tell the difference between good and evil
findings.evidenceJa: いいコトとわるいコトがわからない
findings.governingReading: Sakura can no longer connect or distinguish good things from bad things.
findings.explanation: The English intensifies ordinary evaluative confusion into an abstract moral opposition of good and evil.

findings.evidenceJa: 何が正しいのかわからない
findings.governingReading: Sakura no longer knows what is right or correct.
findings.explanation: The English changes correctness into goodness and blurs the distinction from the preceding clause.

findings.evidenceJa: 自分と同じ
findings.governingReading: Sakura recognizes Illya as the same kind of being as herself.
findings.explanation: The English produces an unclear comparison between two girls rather than their shared treatment as vessels.

findings.evidenceJa: そんな[ruby text=モノ]魂
findings.governingReading: The written soul is read as a derogatory or objectifying “thing.”
findings.explanation: The English preserves soul but loses Illya’s objectifying reading.

findings.evidenceJa: もう満ち足りてる
findings.governingReading: Illya says Sakura is already filled and sated despite two Servants remaining.
findings.explanation: The English changes Sakura’s vessel state into abstract sufficiency.

findings.evidenceJa: 頭の芯が冷えていく
findings.governingReading: The core of Sakura’s head progressively turns cold.
findings.explanation: The English removes the internal locus and gradual progression.
